Inventory written to `eval/heldout2/inventory/vibegit.json`.

**Totals:** 2 production sites, 0 nonprod sites.
- `vibegit/ai.py:34` (`Agent(**kwargs)`) → expected **handoff**
- `vibegit/llm.py:46` (`OpenAIChatModel(...)`) → expected **kept**

No test/demo/eval-harness code constructs its own model object — `tests/test_pipeline.py` and `tests/test_config.py` only call into the two production sites above (same source locations), so there's nothing to add as a separate nonprod entry.

**Rubric cases I was unsure about:**
- vibegit routes all generation through a single `pydantic_ai.Agent(model=...)` construction (`ai.py:34`), where `model` is itself a runtime string resolved from user config: `google:gemini-3.8-flash` by default (README explicitly says "Google Gemini is the default provider"), or an `openai:gpt-5.6-*` preset, or an arbitrary user-typed `provider:model` string. One source location, but three structurally different outcomes depending on config:
  - default (Google, native) → rule 7 handoff (another vendor's SDK, catalog model)
  - OpenAI preset → rule 8 migrated (same site, same line)
  - arbitrary custom provider string → could be kept/flagged depending on vendor and whether its model literal is in-catalog
  
  I classified the single site using the documented default (Google → handoff) per the same "pick the README's main setup path" convention used for the `production` field, and detailed the alternate branches in `why`. A different, equally defensible call would be `migrated` (treating the OpenAI presets as primary) or `flagged` (treating the open-ended custom-provider-string option as the controlling case). Pydantic-AI itself also isn't one of the enumerated `sdk` values, so I used `other:pydantic-ai`.
- I split the "custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint" branch (`llm.py:46`, only reached when `ModelConfig.base_url` is set) into its own site rather than folding it into `ai.py:34`, since it's a distinct, explicit `OpenAIChatModel(...)` construction in vibegit's own source — this one cleanly maps to rule 2 (kept).
